5th Week: 12 - 16 october

Author

Lucía Santos Muñoz

Tuesday 13/10/2026

Pablo sent us the script for the segmentation in StarDist as a extension of QuPath. I installed it with the menu of manage extensions. There, there are defined scripts depending on the image type you have. In our case, it is a H&E 3 channels, RGB. I downloaded the pre-trained model from the git hub they give, and run the script with the parameters Pablo sent (script_nucleus_segmentation.groovy).

def stardist = StarDist2D.builder(modelPath)
    .threshold(0.15)
    .normalizePercentiles(0.1, 99.9)
    .pixelSize(0.25)
    .measureShape()
    .measureIntensity()
    .build()

Also, I cropped the image of the samples 7 and 8, with the script crop_tissue.py.

At the same time I did the alignment of the tiff image and the cytoassist of the samples 1 and 2.

Wednesday 14/10/2026

The run of StarDist extension finished, but in my opinion, there were more detections than real nucleus in the image. So I tried modifying the parameters, the threshold, and the pixel size.

def stardist = StarDist2D
    .builder(modelPath)
    .normalizePercentiles(0.1, 99.9) // Percentile normalization
    .threshold(0.3)              // Probability (detection) threshold
    .pixelSize(0.5)              // Resolution for detection
    .measureShape()              // Add shape measurements
    .measureIntensity()          // Add nucleus measurements
    .build()

This time, the run lasted 25 min, compared to the 5 hours of the last one. And the number of detections increased almost the double comparing to the results of SpaceRanger.

Num Detections 287311

Although the number is better, I think we can improve even more the detections. There are still nucleus that StarDist is not capturing

def stardist = StarDist2D
    .builder(modelPath)
    .normalizePercentiles(0.1, 99.9) // Percentile normalization
    .threshold(0.25)              // Probability (detection) threshold
    .pixelSize(0.5)              // Resolution for detection
    .measureShape()              // Add shape measurements
    .measureIntensity()          // Add nucleus measurements
    .build()

It finished in 25 minutes too, and the total number of detections is: Num Detections 330585

Now, I’m going to launch SpaceRanger with custom segmentations to see the metrics of both geojson. The first hypothesis is than we would have improved de UMIs in cells a 40% (from 43% to aprox. 80%). And in the second, if the improvement is not notorious, the the major detections would be noise.

First, we converted the image sinto pyramidal, by downloading the images from QuPath (it does the conversion automaticly). Then I cleaned the geojson generated with StarDist by modifying the script clean_geojson.py (the paths):

sed -i 's/crop/crop_2/' clean_geojson.py

Then, we tried to launch a SpaceRanger run in the cloud, but it failed due to diferences in the original image and the used to do the fiducial alignment (I used the same, so I don’t know what could happen). So, now I’m going to perform the same analysis but in the terminal.

Thursday 15/10/2026

All the jobs finished, but in the case of TMA_3_4 with the custom alignments, the image and the fiducial alignments were from the complete image. Also, there was a problem with the cluster, the big square was showed as an object, and SR asigned to it a cluster. To solve this, I reloaded the mask in QuPath, removed this square and with the selector I draw all the sample, selecting all te polygons corresponding to nucleus. Finally, I launched again the jobs but with the correct files
